Zak Butters was awarded the Showdown Medal following the Power's win. (Getty Images/AFL Photos: James Elsby)

Port Adelaide duo Zak Butters and Jason Horne-Francis have sparked a 26-point trouncing of Adelaide in one of the great Showdown upsets.

Butters (37 disposals), who was awarded the Showdown Medal, and Horne-Francis (29 disposals, one goal) teamed up to dominate the Crows in the Power's 13.19 (97) to 11.5 (71) triumph at Adelaide Oval on Saturday night.

Speculation is mounting Butters will head home to Victoria at the end of the season.

Butters admitted the thought that the match could be his final Showdown appearance had crossed his mind.

"It definitely did," Butters told Fox Footy.

"Whatever happens, happens at the end of the year … it's so special to play in these games. I love the footy club and I love my teammates and that win makes it extra special."

Forwards Corey Durdin and Mitch Georgiades kicked three goals each and Joe Berry and Jase Burgoyne managed two apiece as15th-placed Power stunned the Crows.

Butters and Horne-Francis were superb as the Power controlled the clearances 42-22. The pair recorded 13 and 10 clearances respectively, more than the entire Crows line-up.

The Power seized command with a stretch of six consecutive majors from midway through the second term, turning a three-point deficit into a commanding 35-point lead early in the third quarter.

Adelaide, now with nine wins and six losses, blew a chance to rise to fourth on the ladder.

Darcy Fogarty booted five goals in a lone attacking hand.

Crows captain Jordan Dawson was subdued despite collecting 25 disposals, and key teammates Izak Rankine (12 disposals) and Josh Rachele (nine disposals, one goal) failed to fire.

The Power's Mitch Zadow kicked the first goal of his AFL career. (Getty Images/AFL Photos: James Elsby)

Rankine limped off late in the first quarter after his right leg was trapped in a Butters tackle.

Rankine's absence came as the Power's won the clearances 16-4 in the opening term but failed to cash in on the scoreboard.

The Power sprayed three set shots at goal and the Crows — with Rachele bouncing through a 40-metre stunner from near a boundary line in a rare Adelaide highlight — led by four points at quarter-time, 4.2 to 3.4.

Rankine returned to action with his right knee strapped in the second term as the Power seized momentum with five goals to two for the quarter.

The Power's small forwards Berry and Durdin slotted two goals each in the quarter as their side skipped 16 points clear at half-time.

They streeted 36 points clear with the initial three goals of the third term in front of a raucous crowd of 50,087 spectators.

The Power held a decisive 33-point advantage at three-quarter time, before closing out victory to narrow their overall Showdown win-loss ledger to 29-31.

Earlier, Carlton notched a sixth straight win under interim coach Josh Fraser with a 53-point triumph over West Coast at Docklands.

Collingwood posted a second consecutive victory with a 34-point defeat of Richmond at the MCG.

Sat 27 Jun 2026 at 11:05pm

By Luke Pentony

That's where we will leave it tonight — thanks for joining us!

A reminder, we will be back for the final two matches of round 16 on Sunday.

Enjoy the rest of your evening!

Sat 27 Jun 2026 at 10:25pm

By Luke Pentony

Key Event

Sat 27 Jun 2026 at 10:20pm

By Luke Pentony

Zak Butters claims the Showdown Medal following a superb display for the victorious Power.

Will this be Butters's last Showdown appearance?

Time will tell, with many commentators expecting he will return to Victoria at the end of the season.

But for now, he'll enjoy the Power's win over their bitter rivals.

Key Event

Sat 27 Jun 2026 at 10:12pm

By Luke Pentony

Power win Showdown 60 by 26 points!

Heading into the match 15th on the ladder, the Power spring an upset over their crosstown rivals.

The match was in the balance for much of the first half, but the Power asserted control and ran out comfortable winners.

Zak Butters was exceptional for the Power with a match-high 37 disposals, while Corey Durdin and Mitch Georgiades each kicked three goals.

Darcy Fogarty was a shining light in a beaten Crows side, kicking five majors.

Jordan Dawson led the disposals count for the Crows with 25.

The Crows had entered the match fifth on the ladder but slip one spot to sixth.

Sat 27 Jun 2026 at 10:08pm

By Luke Pentony

Darcy Fogarty can hold his head high despite the Crows' performance.

Fogarty kicks his fifth goal, although it wil not affect the final result.

Sat 27 Jun 2026 at 10:04pm

By Luke Pentony

We're not far away from full-time in Showdown 60.

The Power are still well on top, leading by 36 points.

Both sides have wasted shots on goal late in the match.

Sat 27 Jun 2026 at 9:53pm

By Luke Pentony

Ben Keays kicks a much-needed goal for the Crows.

A Riley Thilthorpe shot appeared to land over the behind line and bounced back into play.

But Keays was awarded a free kicked and he snapped a goal.

Some confusion followed, along with some boos from the Power fans, but those boos turned to cheers when Mitch Georgiades replied immediately with his third major of the evening.

The Power lead by 35 points.

Sat 27 Jun 2026 at 9:48pm

By Luke Pentony

A score review shows Jason Horne-Francis's long-range effort shaved the post and went through for a behind.

On first viewing it had appeared to be a goal.

Horne-Francis has two behinds to his name early in the final term.

The Power lead by 35 points.

Sat 27 Jun 2026 at 9:41pm

By Luke Pentony

It's the Power leading by 33 points as we make the turn for home.

Can the Power hold on, or will the Crows pull off an almighty comeback?

Key Event

Sat 27 Jun 2026 at 9:35pm

By Luke Pentony

The Power are heading towards the finish line with a 33-point lead in their possession at the final change.

An upset is on the cards!

Sat 27 Jun 2026 at 9:33pm

By Luke Pentony

Zac Taylor lands a set-shot a long way from home, cutting the Power's lead to 33 points.

The Crows need to build on Taylor's effort, although time is running out in the third quarter.

Sat 27 Jun 2026 at 9:30pm

By Luke Pentony

Jase Burgoyne is awarded a mark right in front of the sticks and he makes no mistake with his shot on goal.

Burgoyne now has two majors, helping the Power lead by 39 points.

Sat 27 Jun 2026 at 9:22pm

By Luke Pentony

Darcy Fogarty is doing his best to keep the Crows in the fight.

Fogarty marks strongly and then nails his set-shot to claim his fourth goal of the evening.

The Power now lead by 30.

Sat 27 Jun 2026 at 9:20pm

By Luke Pentony

We're midway through the third quarter, and it's the Power leading by six goals.

The Crows will back their chances of finding a response but they can't leave it too late against this confident Power outfit.

Sat 27 Jun 2026 at 9:10pm

By Luke Pentony

The Power are on fire!

Corey Durdin chips one off his right boot on the run, pushing the Power out to a 35-point lead early in the third term.

Sat 27 Jun 2026 at 9:08pm

By Luke Pentony

Well done Mitch Zadow!

Zadow kicks the first goal of his AFL career, extending the Power's lead over the Crows to 28 points.

A blistering start from the Power in the third quarter!

Sat 27 Jun 2026 at 9:05pm

By Luke Pentony

Xavier Bamert takes an impressive mark and coolly converts from the set-shot to give the Power the best possible start to the third quarter.

The Power lead by 22 points.

Sat 27 Jun 2026 at 9:03pm

By Luke Pentony

Will the Power extend their lead in the third quarter?

Or will the Crows rein in their crosstown rivals?

The second half is underway!

Sat 27 Jun 2026 at 8:57pm

By Luke Pentony

Key Event

Sat 27 Jun 2026 at 8:45pm

By Luke Pentony

There was a bit of heat in that second quarter, with the Power leading at the main break.

They kicked 5.2 to the Crows' 2.0 to establish a 16-point advantage at half-time.
